userStories.title: Executor refusal and partial-outcome errors
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let write previews refuse proposals precisely and approved tools report bounded partial-failure text.

**Motivation** — A preview can only refuse with `not_found`.

**Approach** — **2b1-D1 Preview refusals.** The executor maps two more exceptions thrown by a write tool's `preview`:
- `ToolInputError(reason)` answers `invalid_input: <reason>`, audit outcome `invalid_input`.
- `ToolForbiddenError(need)` answers `forbidden: <tool> needs <need> on <projectSlug>`, audit outcome `forbidden`. This is the text format `execParsed` already uses for an ability refusal.
- Both stop before `propose`, so no action exists. `NotFoundAppException` keeps answering `not_found`.

**2b1-D2 Partial outcomes.** A tool's `execute` may throw `ToolActionError(text)`. `executeAction` answers `{ ok: false, text }` with `text` capped at `RESULT_CAP_BYTES`, so the action is `FAILED` and its outcome note quotes the text. Every other exception keeps today's mapping. The outcome note keeps its 500-character cap (`NOTE_RESULT_MAX`, `actions/outcome-note.ts:4`), so a long batch result is cut in the note; the action's stored `result` keeps all of it and `koda_get_action` returns it.

Changed — the baseline exists only to locate the code; the target is the interface to implement:
- `apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant-tool.types.ts`
  - Baseline: exports `ToolInputError` only.
  - Target: also exports `ToolForbiddenError` (constructor `(need: string)`, readonly `need`) and `ToolActionError` (constructor `(text: string)`, readonly `text`), both subclasses of `Error`.
- `AssistantToolExecutor.proposeWrite` (`assistant-tool.executor.ts`)
  - Baseline: a `preview` exception other than `NotFoundAppException` answers `error: <tool> failed`.
  - Target: `ToolInputError` answers `invalid_input: <reason>` and `ToolForbiddenError` answers `forbidden: <tool> needs <need> on <slug>` (2b1-D1). Both are recorded with that outcome, and `propose` is not called.
- `AssistantToolExecutor.executeAction`
  - Baseline: `NotFoundAppException` answers `not_found`; anything else answers `error: <tool> failed`.
  - Target: `ToolActionError` answers `{ ok: false, text: capText(error.text, RESULT_CAP_BYTES) }`, with no error log. The other two mappings are unchanged.

**Scope** — In: modify assistant-tool.types.ts and the two executor catches; create write-tool-errors.spec.ts using stub writes and the existing executor harness pattern. Out: US-002 descriptors/helper extraction; US-003 through US-007 real tool factories/registration; changes to approval lifecycle, outcome-note caps or web rendering.

**Interface** — `ToolForbiddenError` (constructor `(need: string)`, readonly `need`) and `ToolActionError` (constructor `(text: string)`, readonly `text`), both subclasses of `Error`. `ToolActionError` answers `{ ok: false, text: capText(error.text, RESULT_CAP_BYTES) }`.

Keep existing parser refusals, tool-call replay, actionScope reauthorization, generic exception logging and NotFoundAppException mappings unchanged. Unit tests use vi stubs and inspect the recorded AssistantToolCall outcome and attached proposer's calls; no database is needed.

userStories.title: Write descriptors and shared tool-input helpers
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Advertise the five bounded, approval-only write tools and extract the two shared action-tool helpers without behavioral changes.

**Motivation** — Today a thread can only propose a comment: the registry holds one write tool (`apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/tools/action-tools.ts:116-130`).

**Approach** — **2b1-D3 Descriptors.** The five descriptors form a new group `WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS`, in the order `koda_create_tickets`, `koda_update_ticket`, `koda_link_tickets`, `koda_add_memory`, `koda_record_decision`. `KODA_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS` spreads it last, after `ACTION_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS`. REPO and PROJECT threads then carry 19 descriptors and WORKSPACE threads 20, under `KODA_TOOL_LIMITS.maxTools` (32). Every description says the change happens only after the user approves it and that the call must not be repeated, as `KODA_ADD_COMMENT` does. The runner refuses the whole tool list when any description exceeds `KODA_TOOL_DESCRIPTION_MAX_CHARS` (2000, `apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.ts`), and a WORKSPACE thread appends its `project` sentence, so every description stays at most 2000 characters after that sentence is appended.

**2b1-D5 Input bounds** (the parser refuses with the named reason):
| Tool | Field | Rule | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `koda_create_tickets` | `tickets` | array of 1 to 20 objects | `tickets` |
| | `tickets[i].type` | one of `BUG`, `ENHANCEMENT`, `TASK`, `QUESTION` | `tickets[i].type` |
| | `tickets[i].title` | string, 1 to 200 characters after trim | `tickets[i].title` |
| | `tickets[i].description` | optional string, at most 4000 characters | `tickets[i].description` |
| | `tickets[i].priority` | optional, one of `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH`, `CRITICAL` | `tickets[i].priority` |
| `koda_update_ticket` | `ref` | `TICKET_REF` | `ref` |
| | `title` | optional string, 1 to 200 characters after trim | `title` |
| | `description` | optional string, at most 4000 characters | `description` |
| | `priority` | optional, one of the four priorities | `priority` |
| | `status` | optional, exactly `IN_PROGRESS` | `status` |
| | (all four absent) | at least one change | `changes` |
| `koda_link_tickets` | `links` | array of 1 to 20 objects | `links` |
| | `links[i].ref` | `TICKET_REF` | `links[i].ref` |
| | `links[i].url` | an absolute `http:` or `https:` URL, at most 2048 characters | `links[i].url` |
| | `links[i].linkType` | optional, one of `url`, `pr`, `commit`, `branch` | `links[i].linkType` |
| `koda_add_memory` | `kind` | one of `FACT`, `PREFERENCE`, `CONSTRAINT`, `INCIDENT_PATTERN` (never `DECISION`) | `kind` |
| | `subject`, `predicate` | string, 1 to 200 characters after trim | `subject`, `predicate` |
| | `object` | optional string, at most 4000 characters | `object` |
| `koda_record_decision` | `topic` | string, 1 to 200 characters after trim | `topic` |
| | `decision` | string, 1 to 4000 characters after trim | `decision` |
| | `rationale` | optional string, at most 4000 characters | `rationale` |

`i` is the zero-based index. The descriptors' JSON schemas carry the same bounds. A parsed value is stored as written: only the trimmed length is judged, as `koda_add_comment` does.

The two input helpers private to `action-tools.ts`, `asRecord` and `ticketPath` (`tools/action-tools.ts:41-48`), move to a new `tools/tool-input.ts` and are exported from there; `action-tools.ts` imports them, unchanged in behaviour.

Other existing assertions remain unchanged. Add the new descriptor and helper behavioral assertions.

**Scope** — In: koda-tool-descriptors.ts/.spec.ts, new tools/tool-input.ts/.spec.ts, and the helper import replacement in action-tools.ts. Out: US-001 error types/executor changes; US-003 through US-007 parsers, previews, execution and registration; runner/protocol edits. Do not extract duplicate helpers from unrelated read-tool groups.

**Interface** — `KODA_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS`: `[...TICKET, ...FLEET, ...KNOWLEDGE, ...ACTION, ...WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS]` (19 entries), plus the exported constants `KODA_CREATE_TICKETS`, `KODA_UPDATE_TICKET`, `KODA_LINK_TICKETS`, `KODA_ADD_MEMORY`, `KODA_RECORD_DECISION` and `WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS`. Export `asRecord` and `ticketPath` with the existing signatures/behavior. Schemas are model-facing guidance; tool stories separately implement the runtime bounds. Preserve required `project` injection and catalog immutability for WORKSPACE threads.

userStories.title: Propose and approve ticket creation batches
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add koda_create_tickets as a registered write tool that proposes 1–20 tickets and creates them in order only on approval.

**Motivation** — The umbrella's example asks include "Turn this brainstorm into tickets" and "Record this decision as an ADR".

**Approach** — **2b-R4** `koda_create_tickets` and `koda_link_tickets` apply their items one at a time, in input order. A failure stops the batch, the action is `FAILED`, and its result names what was already applied.

**2b1-D4 Permissions** mirror each REST route (S5b-R6):
- `koda_create_tickets`: ability `create` `Ticket` (`tickets.controller.ts:168`).

**2b1-D5 Input bounds** (the parser refuses with the named reason):
| Tool | Field | Rule | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `koda_create_tickets` | `tickets` | array of 1 to 20 objects | `tickets` |
| | `tickets[i].type` | one of `BUG`, `ENHANCEMENT`, `TASK`, `QUESTION` | `tickets[i].type` |
| | `tickets[i].title` | string, 1 to 200 characters after trim | `tickets[i].title` |
| | `tickets[i].description` | optional string, at most 4000 characters | `tickets[i].description` |
| | `tickets[i].priority` | optional, one of `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH`, `CRITICAL` | `tickets[i].priority` |

`i` is the zero-based index. The descriptors' JSON schemas carry the same bounds. A parsed value is stored as written: only the trimmed length is judged, as `koda_add_comment` does.

**2b1-D6 Previews.** Every preview is passed through `maskSecrets`, as `koda_add_comment`'s is. Each one names the project slug, and every existing ticket it names is read through the project-scoped `TicketsService.findByRef`, so a foreign or missing ref raises `NotFoundAppException` and answers `not_found` before any action exists. The first lines are fixed:
- `koda_create_tickets`: `Create <n> ticket(s) in <slug>:`, then per ticket `<i+1>. [<type>, <priority>] <title>` (priority defaults to `MEDIUM`). When the ticket has a description, each of its lines follows, indented by four spaces.
- Preview size is accepted as bounded by the input bounds (at most about 85 KB for 20 tickets with full descriptions); previews are not truncated, because the user approves the exact text.

**2b1-D7 Execution** runs as the requester with the action project's role (`ctx.actor`, 2a-D8), through the domain services, so the usual ticket events, timeline rows and outbox events fire.
- `koda_create_tickets` calls `TicketsService.create(slug, { type, title, description, priority }, ctx.actor)` once per ticket, in order. The result is one line per ticket, `created <ref> /<slug>/tickets/<ref>`. When ticket `k` fails, it throws `ToolActionError` whose text is the lines already written, then `failed at ticket <k+1>: <reason>`, where the reason is `not_found` for `NotFoundAppException` and `error` for anything else.

**2b1-D8 Tool groups and files.** Each tool is a factory in its own file under `tools/`: `create-tickets-tool.ts`, `update-ticket-tool.ts`, `link-tickets-tool.ts`, `add-memory-tool.ts` and `record-decision-tool.ts`. `TicketWriteTools` (`tools/ticket-write-tools.ts`) registers the three ticket tools and `MemoryWriteTools` (`tools/memory-write-tools.ts`) the two memory tools, each in `onModuleInit` like `ActionTools`. Both are `AssistantModule` providers.

This story creates createTicketsTool and TicketWriteTools with only the create factory registered; US-004 and US-005 add the other ticket factories. Add TicketWriteTools to assistant.module.ts providers (and its symbol import), without adding Nest module imports. Extend assistant.module.spec.ts with an init()-based no-DB assertion of write kind and create Ticket permission, preserving existing tests. Add the unit factory spec and the per-story PG route/approve integration spec.

Integration tests are one file per story. They enter at the runner tool route `POST /api/fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/tools/<name>?leaseEpoch=<n>` and decide at `POST /api/projects/web/fleet/approvals/:approvalId/decide` (the app's `/api` prefix, as in the fixture), where `approvalId` is the stored `PendingAction`'s `approvalId` (not the action id). The fixtures follow `test/integration/fleet/assistant-action-tools.integration.spec.ts`: `seedFleetHttpWorld`, with the web project's key set to `KODA` so the first ticket is `KODA-1`; DEVELOPER `dev`, VIEWER `viewer`; a RUNNING REPO THREAD job from `seedThreadJobFor`, created by `dev` unless an AC names `viewer`; `FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED=true` before boot. The tests need the compose test DB (`bun run test:db:up`). Run the new integration file under test:scoped so it actually executes in DB mode.

**Scope** — In: create factory/parser/masked preview/serial execution, TicketWriteTools provider, AssistantModule registration and per-story tests. Out: US-001 executor/error definitions; US-002 descriptors/helpers; US-004/005 update/link tools; US-006/007 memory tools; atomic batch creation. US-003 only: a requester without `create` `Ticket` (a VIEWER) is refused by the existing executor ability path (2a US-002 AC-8); this feature adds no AC for it.

**Interface** — `TicketsService.create(projectSlug, dto: CreateTicketDto, principal)`, `findByRef(projectSlug, ref)` and `update(projectSlug, ref, dto: UpdateTicketDto, principal)` — `apps/api/src/tickets/tickets.service.ts:93,178,227`. Mirror `addCommentTool` with exported `createTicketsTool` returning an AssistantTool with `kind: 'write'`, descriptor KODA_CREATE_TICKETS and `{ kind: 'ability', action: 'create', subject: 'Ticket' }`. Use US-001 ToolActionError for partial outcomes and US-002 shared helpers; never execute writes from preview.

userStories.title: Propose ticket edits and permission-checked starts
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add koda_update_ticket for title/description/priority edits and the sole status move to IN_PROGRESS, validating permission and state before proposal and rechecking state at approval.

**Motivation** — `koda_update_ticket` needs to refuse a status the requester may not set, or a move the ticket's state does not allow, before an action exists.

**Approach** — **2b-R3** `koda_update_ticket` may set `status` only to `IN_PROGRESS` (the "start" move). The PATCH path carries no comment, and every other move needs a typed comment (`tickets/state-machine/ticket-transitions.ts:13-31`).

**2b1-D4 Permissions** mirror each REST route (S5b-R6):
- `koda_update_ticket`: ability `update` `Ticket` (`tickets.controller.ts:214`). When `status` is set, the preview also requires `transition` `Ticket`, as `TicketsService.update` does through `assertTransitionPermission`.

**2b1-D5 Input bounds** (the parser refuses with the named reason):
| Tool | Field | Rule | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `koda_update_ticket` | `ref` | `TICKET_REF` | `ref` |
| | `title` | optional string, 1 to 200 characters after trim | `title` |
| | `description` | optional string, at most 4000 characters | `description` |
| | `priority` | optional, one of the four priorities | `priority` |
| | `status` | optional, exactly `IN_PROGRESS` | `status` |
| | (all four absent) | at least one change | `changes` |

The four priorities are `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH`, `CRITICAL`. The descriptors' JSON schemas carry the same bounds. A parsed value is stored as written: only the trimmed length is judged, as `koda_add_comment` does.

**2b1-D6 Previews.** Every preview is passed through `maskSecrets`, as `koda_add_comment`'s is. Each one names the project slug, and every existing ticket it names is read through the project-scoped `TicketsService.findByRef`, so a foreign or missing ref raises `NotFoundAppException` and answers `not_found` before any action exists. The first lines are fixed:
- `koda_update_ticket`: `Update <ref> "<title>" in <slug>:`, then one line per changed field in the order `title`, `description`, `priority`, `status`. Title, priority and status read `<field>: <current> -> <new>`. A description change reads `description:` followed by the new text, each line indented by four spaces; the old text is not shown.
- `koda_update_ticket` with `status` checks the requester's `transition` permission before the ticket's current status, so a requester without it gets `forbidden` whatever the status.
- Preview size is accepted as bounded by the input bounds (at most about 85 KB for 20 tickets with full descriptions); previews are not truncated, because the user approves the exact text.

**2b1-D7 Execution** runs as the requester with the action project's role (`ctx.actor`, 2a-D8), through the domain services, so the usual ticket events, timeline rows and outbox events fire.
- `koda_update_ticket` first reads the ticket. When `status` is set and the ticket's current status cannot move to `IN_PROGRESS` (`validateTransition` throws), it throws `ToolActionError('<ref> cannot move from <status> to IN_PROGRESS')` before any write. Otherwise it calls `TicketsService.update(slug, ref, changes, ctx.actor)`, and the result is `updated <ref> /<slug>/tickets/<ref>`. A `ForbiddenAppException` from the service becomes `ToolActionError('forbidden: <ref> needs transition Ticket')`.

Failure handling:
- `status` set and the requester lacks `transition` `Ticket`: Preview throws `ToolForbiddenError('transition Ticket')`; `forbidden: koda_update_ticket needs transition Ticket on <slug>`; no action.
- `status` set and the ticket cannot start from its current status: Preview throws `ToolInputError('status')`; `invalid_input: status`; no action.
- Ticket changed between proposal and approval so it can no longer start: `FAILED`, result `<ref> cannot move from <status> to IN_PROGRESS`; nothing written.

Create update-ticket-tool.ts/.spec.ts and assistant-update-ticket-tool.integration.spec.ts. Register updateTicketTool in the TicketWriteTools provider created by US-003. Extend assistant.module.spec.ts with the write-kind/update Ticket registration check; preserve all existing tests. No new AssistantModule provider or Nest module import is needed. Per-story integration uses US-003's route/decide fixtures: POST /api/fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/tools/koda_update_ticket?leaseEpoch=<n>, then POST /api/projects/web/fleet/approvals/:approvalId/decide with the stored approvalId, not action id. Set FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED=true before boot, project web key KODA, dev DEVELOPER, dev-created RUNNING REPO THREAD job, and explicitly set each test's own ticket status. Use the compose test DB and test:scoped for real integration execution.

**Scope** — In: update parser, masked field-diff preview, transition permission/state refusal, approval-time precheck, domain update call and registration/tests. Out: US-003 creation, US-005 links, US-006/007 memory writes; non-start status moves, typed-comment workflow, assignments/labels/deletion, and locking the race between start check and TicketsService.update. US-004 only: a requester without `update` `Ticket` (a VIEWER) is refused by the existing executor ability path (2a US-002 AC-8); this feature adds no AC for it. US-004 only: a `koda_update_ticket` ref that matches no ticket of the project answers `not_found` through `TicketsService.findByRef` and the existing executor preview mapping, as US-005 AC-6 pins for links; this feature adds no `koda_update_ticket` AC for it.

**Interface** — `TicketsService.create(projectSlug, dto: CreateTicketDto, principal)`, `findByRef(projectSlug, ref)` and `update(projectSlug, ref, dto: UpdateTicketDto, principal)` — `apps/api/src/tickets/tickets.service.ts:93,178,227`. `TicketTransitionsService.assertTransitionPermission(principal)` — throws `ForbiddenAppException` without `transition` `Ticket` (`tickets/state-machine/ticket-transitions.service.ts:518`). `validateTransition(from, to, commentType?)` — throws `ValidationAppException` for a move with no rule (`tickets/state-machine/ticket-transitions.ts:39`). Export updateTicketTool as an AssistantTool using KODA_UPDATE_TICKET, kind write and `{ kind: 'ability', action: 'update', subject: 'Ticket' }`. Do not include ref in the changes DTO, and do not call assertTransitionPermission for field-only previews. Use validateTransition without a comment to reject VERIFY_FIX as well as terminal/self transitions.

userStories.title: Propose ordered ticket URL link batches
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add koda_link_tickets as a member-permitted write tool for attaching 1–20 URLs to project tickets after approval.

**Motivation** — The 2a write contract is generic — `kind: 'write'`, `preview`, `execute` (`apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant-tool.types.ts:18-33`) — so each new tool is a descriptor, a parser, a preview and an execute.

**Approach** — **2b-R4** `koda_create_tickets` and `koda_link_tickets` apply their items one at a time, in input order. A failure stops the batch, the action is `FAILED`, and its result names what was already applied.

**2b1-D4 Permissions** mirror each REST route (S5b-R6):
- `koda_link_tickets`: project membership. The link route checks only membership (`ticket-links.controller.ts:57`). This corrects the umbrella §7 row, which named the ticket abilities.

**2b1-D5 Input bounds** (the parser refuses with the named reason):
| Tool | Field | Rule | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `koda_link_tickets` | `links` | array of 1 to 20 objects | `links` |
| | `links[i].ref` | `TICKET_REF` | `links[i].ref` |
| | `links[i].url` | an absolute `http:` or `https:` URL, at most 2048 characters | `links[i].url` |
| | `links[i].linkType` | optional, one of `url`, `pr`, `commit`, `branch` | `links[i].linkType` |

`i` is the zero-based index. The descriptors' JSON schemas carry the same bounds. A parsed value is stored as written: only the trimmed length is judged, as `koda_add_comment` does.

**2b1-D6 Previews.** Every preview is passed through `maskSecrets`, as `koda_add_comment`'s is. Each one names the project slug, and every existing ticket it names is read through the project-scoped `TicketsService.findByRef`, so a foreign or missing ref raises `NotFoundAppException` and answers `not_found` before any action exists. The first lines are fixed:
- `koda_link_tickets`: `Link <n> URL(s) in <slug>:`, then per link `- <ref> "<title>" <- <linkType> <url>`. `linkType` is the one given, or the one `TicketLinksService.inferLinkType` would infer, copied into the tool because that method is private: `pr` when the URL matches `/\/pull\/\d+/`, `/\/merge_requests\/\d+/` or `/\/pull-requests\/\d+/`, else `url`.
- Preview size is accepted as bounded by the input bounds (at most about 85 KB for 20 tickets with full descriptions); previews are not truncated, because the user approves the exact text.

**2b1-D7 Execution** runs as the requester with the action project's role (`ctx.actor`, 2a-D8), through the domain services, so the usual ticket events, timeline rows and outbox events fire.
- `koda_link_tickets` calls `TicketLinksService.create(slug, ref, { url, linkType })` once per link, in order. The result is one line per link, `linked <ref> <url>` with ` (already linked)` appended when the service answered status 200. A failure at link `k` throws `ToolActionError` with the lines so far, then `failed at link <k+1>: <reason>`.

The failure reason follows the batch rule: `not_found` for NotFoundAppException and `error` for anything else. A URL already linked to the ticket is not a failure: that line reads `linked <ref> <url> (already linked)`; the batch continues. A ref that is not a ticket of the project answers `not_found`; no action. Do not leak raw exception details.

Add linkTicketsTool to the existing TicketWriteTools.onModuleInit and extend assistant.module.spec.ts with a write-kind/member registration assertion, preserving existing tests. Integration follows the upstream assistant-create-tickets-tool.integration.spec.ts fixture, entering at POST /api/fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/tools/koda_link_tickets?leaseEpoch=<n> and deciding at POST /api/projects/web/fleet/approvals/:approvalId/decide with stored approvalId (not action id). **Interface** — `TicketLinksService.create(slug, ref, dto: CreateTicketLinkDto): Promise<{ status: 200 | 201; link }>` — answers 200 for a URL already linked to the ticket (`ticket-links/ticket-links.service.ts`). `TICKET_REF` — `fleet/assistant/tools/ticket-tools.ts:23`. `maskSecrets` — `fleet/assistant/assistant-tool-safety.ts`. | | `subject`, `predicate` | string, 1 to 200 characters after trim | `subject`, `predicate` |
| | `object` | optional string, at most 4000 characters | `object` |

**2b1-D6 Previews.** Every preview is passed through `maskSecrets`, as `koda_add_comment`'s is. This is an additive enhancement of S5b-2a, not greenfield. Navigation: codebase-memory MCP is not exposed in this session, so discovery used direct Read/Grep/Glob against the supplied execution root. No implementation code was changed and no tests were executed while drafting this PRD. The detected Express/Next.js labels in the prompt are not authoritative: the API context specifies NestJS 12 with Fastify, Prisma 7/Postgres, Nathapp platform services, Vitest and oxlint (.nax/mono/apps/api/context.md:17); package dependencies corroborate Nest/Fastify (apps/api/package.json:59). All seven stories are scoped to apps/api. Read the app context and nathapp-nestjs-patterns skill before implementing Nest code; preserve existing Nathapp exception, DI and response-envelope conventions.

Existing write architecture and consumers: AssistantTool<I> already has kind, preview, parse and execute (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant-tool.types.ts:18); ToolContext supplies projectId/projectSlug, the requester actor, thread/job and a safe data formatter (:7). Only ToolInputError currently exists (:39). AssistantToolExecutor.executeAction re-resolves the requester and action project's membership/ability through actionScope, reparses stored input, runs execute and caps successes at RESULT_CAP_BYTES=16384 (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant-tool.executor.ts:19,81,98). Its current catch maps NotFoundAppException to not_found and all other exceptions to a logged generic failure. execParsed already performs the declared CASL tuple check (:228). REPO/PROJECT use the home project; WORKSPACE strips its project argument after resolving the named project and membership (:195), so factories must use ctx.projectId and ctx.projectSlug rather than assume the thread's home project. proposeWrite calls preview instead of execute, then passes the parsed input and preview to ActionProposer (:266); currently only NotFoundAppException gets a specific preview refusal. US-001 adds ToolForbiddenError/ToolActionError to the existing types file despite that file being omitted from the spec's abbreviated Modifies list, and adds only the two preview mappings and the partial-action mapping to the executor. Preserve existing parsing, idempotent tool-call replay, audit storage, permission gates, generic error logging, caps and not_found behavior. ToolActionError is expected failure data and must not be error-logged. Existing call outcome values already support invalid_input/forbidden; no schema change is needed.

Approval lifecycle must stay untouched: AssistantActionDecisions checks that the caller is the requester, reauthorizes an approve, commits APPROVED before executeAction and finalizes afterwards (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/actions/assistant-action-decisions.ts:69,96,140). finalize writes FAILED for ok:false, stores the capped result and inserts the outcome note in the same finalization transaction (:140). Approval itself remains approved even when the action fails. outcomeNote already quotes failure text and uses NOTE_RESULT_MAX=500 (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/actions/outcome-note.ts:4,17). getActionTool reads only the calling project's/thread's action and returns its stored result using ctx.data (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/tools/action-tools.ts:89,107). The full stored result means the RESULT_CAP_BYTES-bounded text, not unlimited output; notes keep the existing 500-character result cap. No outcome-note, web card or inbox implementation changes are required.

Tool pattern and catalog impact: addCommentTool implements hand parsing, allowlisted parsed fields, masked preview, domain-service execution and a declared write permission; ActionTools registers factories onModuleInit (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/tools/action-tools.ts:45,116). Move only that file's asRecord and ticketPath to tools/tool-input.ts unchanged (:34,39); do not sweep duplicate private helpers in unrelated groups. New factories each live in their own file and register through TicketWriteTools (created in US-003, extended in US-004/005) and MemoryWriteTools (created in US-006, extended in US-007). AssistantModule already imports TicketsModule, TicketLinksModule and MemoryModule (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant.module.ts:35); add provider symbols and their TypeScript imports, not new Nest module imports. TicketsModule exports both services needed for updates (apps/api/src/tickets/tickets.module.ts:25); MemoryModule exports PrismaMemoryItemRepository and ExtractionService (apps/api/src/memory/memory.module.ts:45). The registry registration seam is proven by module.init(), not compile() alone (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant.module.spec.ts:50). Each story adds a write-kind/permission registration assertion without weakening existing tests.

KODA_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS currently ends in ACTION_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/koda-tool-descriptors.ts:326,329). US-002 appends the five exported descriptors as WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS, preserving all earlier groups and object identity. withProjectArgument appends a sentence and required project schema without mutating catalog entries (:360), so schemas must work both directly and under WORKSPACE wrapping. Catalog tests explicitly assert the old suffix, counts and pre-action prefix; change precisely those anchors and add the new descriptor assertions (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/koda-tool-descriptors.spec.ts:133,141,157). Placement imports kodaToolDescriptorsFor and copies its result into THREAD ASSIGN (apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/placement.service.ts:10,227); its project-code spec compares WORKSPACE against that function (:181). The runner rejects an entire list if a description is over 2000 characters, including the workspace sentence, or the list is over maxTools (apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.ts:88,97,105). The final 19 REPO/PROJECT and 20 WORKSPACE descriptors fit the 32-tool limit. Descriptors can exist before their dependent registrations during development; ship the completed story chain together. No runner or shared-protocol edits. API fleet-protocol imports must remain type-only, following existing catalog code.

Tickets and links: TicketsService.create uses per-project number allocation/retry, CREATED/default MEDIUM and actorForeignKeys, and emits the normal ticket event/outbox within its transaction (apps/api/src/tickets/tickets.service.ts:93). findByRef performs a single project/key-scoped lookup and excludes soft-deleted records (:178); all existing-ticket previews must call it to avoid cross-project disclosure. TICKET_REF rejects CUIDs, lowercase keys and leading-zero numbers (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/tools/ticket-tools.ts:23). TicketsService.update checks transition permission before applying fields, then invokes the state machine (:227). assertTransitionPermission fails closed and enforces transition Ticket (apps/api/src/tickets/state-machine/ticket-transitions.service.ts:518). validateTransition uses typed-comment rules; CREATED/VERIFIED can start without a comment but VERIFY_FIX cannot, even though it has an IN_PROGRESS edge (apps/api/src/tickets/state-machine/ticket-transitions.ts:13,39). US-004 must check transition permission before validating the current status, and recheck the current state at approval. Do not replace state-machine/service behavior with direct Prisma writes. The remaining race between start precheck and the service's field update/transition is explicitly accepted, not a locking project. TicketLinksService.create resolves the scoped ticket, returns status 200 for an existing URL or 201 for a new link, and infers only pr versus url unless explicit linkType is given (apps/api/src/ticket-links/ticket-links.service.ts:53,69). inferLinkType is private, so the preview must copy exactly its three PR URL patterns, not expand inference for commit/branch URLs. DTO validation does not execute when calling services directly, so the tool parser must enforce all specified limits and enums (apps/api/src/ticket-links/dto/create-ticket-link.dto.ts:4). Create/link batches await each item in input order and stop at the first failure, retaining earlier writes and reporting only not_found or error, never raw exception text. There is deliberately no enclosing batch transaction, rollback or retry.

Memory and decisions: memory REST authorization is membership-based; its admin override is intentionally stricter in these tools, which always attribute to ctx.actor.id (apps/api/src/memory/memory.controller.ts:31,103,145). Parsers must build allowlisted outputs so ownerId/actorId cannot survive into PendingAction.input, including for admins. PrismaMemoryItemRepository.upsert is a serializable transaction that deduplicates identical source/object replays and supersedes the current active kind/subject/predicate key, then saves owner and source metadata (apps/api/src/memory/prisma-memory-item.repository.ts:155). findActive is project/key/status scoped (:215); reuse it for replacement previews without changing repository semantics. recordDecision keys decisions as agent:<actorId> and topic, supersedes that requester's active decision and stores only input.decision as object, ignoring rationale (apps/api/src/memory/extraction.service.ts:204,223). US-007 must append a given rationale to decision with two newlines and Rationale: before calling the existing service, passing no rationale field and the same repository. Preserve the service's decision_event source type, confidence and supersession behavior; only sourceId is thread:<threadId>. A generic memory uses sourceType thread and bare threadId, confidence 0.8. Do not change these read-only domain integrations or broaden writes to legacy RAG. memorySearchTool already reads through MemoryGovernanceService with projectId and returns fenced memory:<id> rows (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/tools/knowledge-tools.ts:133). US-006's route-level readback proves this write/read seam. Repository and extraction failures may still produce existing generic failures; do not introduce new retry or atomicity guarantees.

Tests and execution: executor tests already provide stub tools, in-memory call audit rows, attached proposers and PendingAction fixtures (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant-tool.executor.spec.ts:24,66,96). Add write-tool-errors.spec.ts for US-001 rather than rewriting their harness behavior. Descriptor/helper tests cover US-002. All new tool unit specs use mocked domain services. DI tests remain no-DB units in assistant.module.spec.ts; its existing GlobalStubsModule compilation and init pattern is the baseline (:20,51). Existing domain regression suites include tickets.service.spec.ts, ticket-transitions.service.spec.ts/ticket-transitions.spec.ts, ticket-links.service.spec.ts, memory.controller.spec.ts and extraction.service.spec.ts. Each tool story creates its own integration file. assistant-action-tools.integration.spec.ts supplies seedFleetHttpWorld, KODA key setup, runner enrollment, route envelope extraction and real proposals (apps/api/test/integration/fleet/assistant-action-tools.integration.spec.ts:61,92). Approval examples use stored approvalId, not action id (apps/api/test/integration/fleet/assistant-actions-approve.integration.spec.ts:56; assistant-actions-decide.integration.spec.ts:59). seedThreadJobFor defaults to dev's RUNNING REPO THREAD job with leaseEpoch 1 and supports a viewer creator (apps/api/test/helpers/thread-fixtures.ts:42). Set FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED=true before boot, use /api/fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/tools/<name>?leaseEpoch=<n>, and decide at /api/projects/web/fleet/approvals/:approvalId/decide as dev. Set CREATED or VERIFY_FIX explicitly on each test's own ticket; do not rely on another test's status. Avoid shared pending-action cap interference between cases. Use generated Prisma client types, vi rather than jest, and lazy import for TypeScript modules. bun run test excludes integration/e2e; bun run test:scoped selects DB mode for their paths (apps/api/package.json:13,20). Integration requires real Postgres and KODA_DB_TESTS=1; bring up compose using bun run test:db:up from apps/api outside the Docker-less agent sandbox. DB tests reset their database: do not run DB-mode suites concurrently against the same database. Generated acceptance material stays under .nax and must not be edited/copied into src.

Scope, migration and fidelity: exact binding dependencies are retained: US-001 and US-002 independent, US-003 depends on both, then US-004 through US-007 serially. This also avoids conflicting registration/module edits. No Prisma schema, migrations, REST controller/DTO contract, OpenAPI, generated client, CLI, web, runner or protocol-version changes. Existing pending comment actions and all read tools keep their previous behavior. Ship by extending types/executor and catalog first, then registering each factory/provider in dependency order. Primary risks are executing before approval, cross-project lookup leakage, accidentally granting update via membership, checking state before transition permission, exposing admin attribution overrides, losing rationale, mismatched schemas/parsers, result-byte versus preview-character truncation, hiding partial writes, and descriptor descriptions invalidating an ASSIGN. Preview text is masked but not capped; inputs are retained as written after trimmed-length validation, not normalized, and result caps must never be applied to previews. All 89 numbered spec ACs remain in their original stories. Additional acceptance assertions below come only from explicit Failure Handling rows (precise refusal/no action, late-state failure, partial batch FAILED results), not invented edge cases. Failure-table rows for VIEWER create/update ability refusals, update missing refs and deleted-before-approval retain the existing executor/service mappings; the explicit Out of Scope says this feature adds no AC for those cases, so those exclusions take precedence over expanding the table into new tool-specific ACs. No speculative criteria are promoted into acceptanceCriteria. Refine-pass audit: enumerated and matched every numbered spec criterion to the same-position criterion in its original story: US-001 AC-1 through AC-9 (preview input refusal/result, no proposal, invalid_input audit; forbidden result, no proposal, forbidden audit; partial action text, byte cap, unchanged plain-error mapping); US-002 AC-1 through AC-13 (ordered five descriptors, final-five placement, preceding action pair, REPO count, WORKSPACE count, approval phrase, workspace description cap, tickets bounds, links bounds, start-only enum, non-decision enum, array helper refusal, ticket path); US-003 AC-1 through AC-14 (empty batch, oversized batch, indexed bad type, indexed blank title, preview heading, default priority, masked secret, ordered create arguments, success lines, partial failure text, create permission registration, runner pending response, approved titles in order, requester creator attribution); US-004 AC-1 through AC-15 (no changes, invalid status, preview heading, priority diff, field-only permission bypass, transition refusal adapter, VERIFY_FIX refusal, update arguments, result text, late CLOSED failure, no update after that failure, service forbidden adapter, update permission registration, real preview refusal route, approved status/priority); US-005 AC-1 through AC-15 (empty batch, oversized batch, FTP refusal, bad link type, inferred PR preview, same scoped not-found exception, ordered link service arguments, already-linked result, new-link result, partial not-found text, member registration, runner pending, no link before approval, approved inferred PR link, viewer membership permission); US-006 AC-1 through AC-12 (DECISION refusal, blank subject, owner override stripped, preview, replacement with object, replacement without object, upsert arguments, saved result, member registration, runner pending, no premature memory, approved search readback); US-007 AC-1 through AC-11 (blank decision, actor override stripped, rationale preview, requester/topic lookup, supersession preview, rationale storage arguments, decision-only arguments, result text, member registration, runner pending, one requester-owned active decision with full stored text). Thus all 89 numbered ACs and their qualifying clauses remain; the nine explicit failure-table supplements follow those blocks, for 98 total. In particular, preserve US-005 AC-15's membership-is-enough parenthetical, US-006 AC-3/US-007 AC-2's 2b-R5 qualifiers, the same-exception qualification in US-005 AC-6, and the already-linked suffix. Each criterion is observable via results, exceptions, mock call arguments or persisted state. Every story has a negative path: US-002 AC-12 is specifically malformed array input returning an empty record; the other six have explicit input or execution failures. Backward compatibility is anchored by US-001 AC-9 and US-002 AC-3/12/13 plus the unchanged existing prefix/identity/module tests specified in descriptions. No deprecated grep/file/verbatim AC tags occur. All 18 top-level out-of-scope items were compared item by item and retained verbatim; no story-local deferrals were hoisted. Binding story ids, workdirs and dependencies are unchanged. Context audit restores US-004's explicitly recommended upstream create-ticket integration fixture within its five-file limit; all other critical spec context entries are already present and no story lists its own outputs as context. Factories follow the existing ActionTools/provider pattern and reuse already imported/exported services, so US-003/004/006 are medium rather than complex; strict three-session-tdd remains mandatory for their permission/ownership code. US-002 remains medium/tdd-simple for catalog and unchanged helper extraction. The late-state failure supplement now names CLOSED/MEDIUM explicitly instead of an unspecified set of unchanged fields, and applies before service entry, not to the excluded check/update race. Rechecked domain interfaces confirm no actor argument to TicketLinksService.create, a bare threadId source for generic memory, thread:<threadId> for decisions, and rationale embedded only in the decision string.
outOfScope: `koda_add_kb_doc` and any write to the RAG knowledge base: dropped by ruling 2b-R2.
Status moves other than the start move to `IN_PROGRESS` (verify, fix, verify-fix, close, reject): they need typed comments the tool does not take (2b-R3).
Assigning, unassigning, labelling or deleting tickets through a tool.
Ticket-to-ticket relations (blocks, depends on, duplicates): koda has no such model; `koda_link_tickets` attaches URLs only.
Creating a batch of tickets or links atomically; items apply one at a time and a failure leaves the earlier ones in place (2b-R4).
Attributing a memory item or decision to anyone other than the requester, including for global admins (2b-R5).
Writing a `DECISION` memory item through `koda_add_memory`; decisions go through `koda_record_decision` only.
Any web change: the thread card, the inbox panel and the system notes already render every write tool from its preview text.
Changes to the runner, the fleet protocol or `FLEET_PROTOCOL_VERSION`.
Editing a proposed action's input before deciding it (umbrella §12).
Storing a decision's rationale in a field of its own; it is appended to the stored decision text (2b1-D7).
Annotating the ticket, link or memory events with `via: thread <id>`; the approval activity row carries the thread id, and memory rows carry it as `sourceId`.
US-003 only: a requester without `create` `Ticket` (a VIEWER) is refused by the existing executor ability path (2a US-002 AC-8); this feature adds no AC for it.
US-004 only: a requester without `update` `Ticket` (a VIEWER) is refused by the existing executor ability path (2a US-002 AC-8); this feature adds no AC for it.

US-004 only: a `koda_update_ticket` ref that matches no ticket of the project answers `not_found` through `TicketsService.findByRef` and the existing executor preview mapping, as US-005 AC-6 pins for links; this feature adds no `koda_update_ticket` AC for it.
A ticket deleted between proposal and approval answers `not_found` through the existing `executeAction` mapping; this feature adds no AC for it.

US-004 only: a ticket whose status changes between the start check and `TicketsService.update` can leave the field changes written and the transition refused; the window is one request and is not locked.
